course_name_original: Diseño y Análisis Avanzado de Sistemas Mecatrónicos
course_name_en: Advanced Design and Analysis of Mechatronic Systems
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of different machine elements, their appropriate selection and calculation, or be concurrently studying subjects to acquire this knowledge.
CAD/CAE course from the first semester of the first year of the master's, or equivalent knowledge acquired in the undergraduate degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge and problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader or multidisciplinary contexts related to Mechanics.

Integrate such knowledge and address the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the responsibilities associated with the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Communicate conclusions (as well as the knowledge and reasons supporting them) to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continued self-directed or autonomous study.

Develop technical specifications that allow for posing a mechatronic engineering problem while maintaining a global and integrating vision and using prescriptive, procedural, or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Evaluate the viability of new mechatronic products, based on their technological characteristics, manufacturing possibilities, and other socio-economic factors related to their possible implementation.

Know and use finite element simulation software to study the integral behavior (mechanical, static and dynamic, thermal, magnetic, electrical, etc.) of mechatronic elements and correctly interpret the results.
Select the material, size, and optimize the shape of mechatronic system elements, taking into account criteria of resistance, durability, and reliability.
Plan the assembly, commissioning, and maintenance of mechatronic equipment or system.
Understand regulations and apply quality management techniques and tools in the design of mechatronic equipment and systems.
Know and apply advanced calculation methods and FEA software for the calculation of mechanical components.
Know and apply functional design processes (from conceptual design to detailed design) and functional optimization of mechanical components.
Analyze vibrations in rotating elements and identify possible manufacturing, assembly, or operational defects.
Know and apply techniques for measuring unbalance and balancing rotating elements.
Know and apply shaft alignment techniques in machines.
Know and design in accordance with current machine safety regulations.

syllabus_topics: Advanced use of FEA software in mechanical systems
Conceptual and detailed design of mechanical systems

assessment_methods.method: Objective test (written and practical computer-based exam)
Assignments and projects (activities from laboratory practices involving calculations, designs, and technical documentation)

assessment_rules: In ordinary examination, the final grade is based on a 60% objective test and 40% assignments and projects. The objective test will be a theoretical-practical exam including a written and a practical computer part. In extraordinary examination, 100% of the grade will be an objective theoretical-practical test covering all course content, including laboratory practices.
